records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying: (L); came to me: (B); {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this formula, which opens each new oracle in chapters 12-15. As at 11:14, the oracle that follows is not put in quotation marks; only words quoted within it are.

records.heading: Baggage for exile

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם בְּת֥וֹךְ בֵּית־הַמֶּ֖רִי אַתָּ֣ה יֹשֵׁ֑ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֵינַיִם֩ לָהֶ֨ם לִרְא֜וֹת וְלֹ֣א רָא֗וּ אָזְנַ֨יִם לָהֶ֤ם לִשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ וְלֹ֣א שָׁמֵ֔עוּ כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽם׃
records.gloss: Son of man, in [the] midst of the house of rebellion you [are] living, who [have] eyes to see but do not see, ears to hear but do not hear, for a house of rebellion they [are].
pieces: Son of man, you live among a rebellious house. They have eyes that can see, yet they do not see, and ears that can hear, yet they do not hear, because they are a rebellious house.

L.2: Son of man, you are living in the midst of the house of rebellion, who have eyes to see but do not see, who have ears to hear but do not hear; for they [are] a house of rebellion.

R.2: Son of man, you are living among people who refuse to obey. They have eyes that could see, but they do not see. They have ears that could hear, but they do not hear. They are people who refuse to obey.

decisions.choice: the house of rebellion: Ezekiel's name for Israel (see 2:5)
decisions.reason: See 2:5. The phrase frames the verse, at its start and its end.

decisions.choice: eyes to see but do not see, ears to hear but do not hear: the charge of Isaiah 6:9-10 and Jeremiah 5:21
decisions.reason: The people can see and hear but will not take in what they see and hear. Jeremiah 5:21 uses nearly the same words, and Jesus takes them up in Mark 8:18. The sign that follows is acted out for people who will not listen to words.

decisions.choice: house of rebellion (L); rebellious house (B); people who refuse to obey (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this phrase in Ezekiel (see 2:5).

records.source: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ כְּלֵ֣י גוֹלָ֔ה וּגְלֵ֥ה יוֹמָ֖ם לְעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְגָלִ֨יתָ מִמְּקוֹמְךָ֜ אֶל־מָק֤וֹם אַחֵר֙ לְעֵ֣ינֵיהֶ֔ם אוּלַ֣י יִרְא֔וּ כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: And you, son of man, make for yourself baggage of exile, and go into exile by day in their sight; and you will go into exile from your place to another place in their sight. Perhaps they will see, for a house of rebellion they [are].
pieces: So you, son of man, pack your belongings for exile, and in daylight, while they watch, set out as one going into exile. Go from your place to another place while they watch. Perhaps they will understand, rebellious house though they are.

L.3: And you, son of man, make for yourself an exile's baggage, and go into exile by day before their eyes; you shall go into exile from your place to another place before their eyes. Perhaps they will see, though they [are] a house of rebellion.

R.3: So, son of man, pack your things as if you were being taken away as a captive. Then, in the daytime, while they are watching, leave your home and go to another place. Maybe they will understand, even though they are people who refuse to obey.

decisions.choice: an exile's baggage: the few things a deportee could carry
decisions.reason: People taken into exile could take only what they could carry on their backs (compare Jeremiah 46:19). Ezekiel is to pack such a bundle and carry it out in plain view.

decisions.choice: a sign acted out: Ezekiel's actions carry the message
decisions.reason: Like the signs of 4:1-5:4, this is a message performed rather than spoken. Ezekiel, already an exile in Babylon, acts out the exile still to come for those left in Jerusalem (12:10-11).

decisions.choice: perhaps they will see, though they are rebellious
alternatives: perhaps they will see that they are a rebellious house
decisions.reason: The word joining the last clause can mean "though" or "for", and it can also introduce what they might see: that they are a rebellious house. The sense of hope against the odds is the same.

decisions.choice: as if you were being taken away as a captive
alternatives: an exile's baggage; go into exile
decisions.reason: Readable explains what going into exile means, since the word "exile" may not be known to young readers.

records.source: וְהוֹצֵאתָ֨ כֵלֶ֜יךָ כִּכְלֵ֥י גוֹלָ֛ה יוֹמָ֖ם לְעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְאַתָּ֗ה תֵּצֵ֤א בָעֶ֨רֶב֙ לְעֵ֣ינֵיהֶ֔ם כְּמוֹצָאֵ֖י גּוֹלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And bring out your baggage like baggage of exile by day in their sight; and you, go out in the evening in their sight, like those going out [into] exile.
pieces: Bring out your belongings by day while they watch, like belongings packed for exile. Then in the evening, while they watch, go out yourself like people going into exile.

L.4: And you shall bring out your baggage like an exile's baggage by day before their eyes; and you yourself shall go out in the evening before their eyes, like those who go out into exile.

R.4: During the day, while they are watching, bring out your things packed as if for exile. Then in the evening, while they are watching, leave like a captive being taken away.

decisions.choice: by day, the baggage; in the evening, the man himself
decisions.reason: The bundle goes out in daylight so that all can see it; Ezekiel himself leaves at dusk, as people fleeing or being led away would leave (12:12).

records.source: לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם חֲתָר־לְךָ֣ בַקִּ֑יר וְהוֹצֵאתָ֖ בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: In their sight dig for yourself through the wall, and bring out through it.
pieces: As they look on, dig a hole in the wall and take your belongings out through it.

L.5: Before their eyes dig for yourself through the wall, and bring [it] out through it.

R.5: While they are watching, dig a hole through the wall of your house and carry your things out through it.

decisions.choice: dig through the wall: the wall of his house, made of mud brick
decisions.reason: Houses in Babylonia were built of mud brick, which could be dug through by hand (compare Job 24:16). The act pictures people escaping from a city by a hole in the wall, as the king will do (12:12).

decisions.choice: the wall of your house
decisions.reason: Readable says which wall is meant (m1).

records.source: לְעֵ֨ינֵיהֶ֜ם עַל־כָּתֵ֤ף תִּשָּׂא֙ בָּעֲלָטָ֣ה תוֹצִ֔יא פָּנֶ֣יךָ תְכַסֶּ֔ה וְלֹ֥א תִרְאֶ֖ה אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־מוֹפֵ֥ת נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: In their sight on [the] shoulder you shall lift, in the darkness bring out; your face you shall cover, and not see the land; for a sign I have made you to [the] house of Israel.
pieces: While they watch, lift the bundle onto your shoulder and carry it out in the dark. Cover your face so that you do not see the land, for I have made you a sign for the house of Israel.

L.6: Before their eyes you shall lift [it] onto [your] shoulder; in the dark you shall carry [it] out. You shall cover your face so that you do not see the land, for a sign I have made you to the house of Israel.

R.6: While they are watching, put your bundle on your shoulder and carry it out in the dark. Cover your face so that you cannot see the land. I have made you a sign to warn the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: a sign: an act that points to what will happen
decisions.reason: The word is used for a sign or portent, a person or deed that shows ahead of time what God will do (24:24, 27; Isaiah 8:18; 20:3).

decisions.choice: cover your face so that you do not see the land: the grief and shame of leaving, and the king's fate
decisions.reason: Covering the face is a sign of mourning and shame (2 Samuel 15:30; 19:5). It also looks ahead to the king who "will not see the land" (12:12-13).

decisions.choice: a sign to warn
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sign is for.

records.source: וָאַ֣עַשׂ כֵּן֮ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צֻוֵּיתִי֒ כֵּ֠לַי הוֹצֵ֜אתִי כִּכְלֵ֤י גוֹלָה֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וּבָעֶ֛רֶב חָתַֽרְתִּי־לִ֥י בַקִּ֖יר בְּיָ֑ד בָּעֲלָטָ֥ה הוֹצֵ֛אתִי עַל־כָּתֵ֥ף נָשָׂ֖אתִי לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And I did so, as I had been commanded; my baggage I brought out like baggage of exile by day, and in the evening I dug for myself through the wall with [the] hand; in the darkness I brought out; on [the] shoulder I carried in their sight.
pieces: So I did as I was commanded. By day I brought out my belongings as if packed for exile, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my hands. I took them out in the dark, carrying them on my shoulder while they watched.

L.7: And I did so, as I had been commanded. My baggage I brought out like an exile's baggage by day, and in the evening I dug for myself through the wall with [my] hand; in the dark I brought [it] out; on [my] shoulder I carried [it] before their eyes.

R.7: So I did what I was told. During the day I brought out my things packed as if for exile. In the evening I dug through the wall with my hands. Then I went out in the dark, carrying my bundle on my shoulder while the people watched.

decisions.choice: I did as I had been commanded: the sign is carried out in every detail
decisions.reason: Ezekiel repeats each part of the command (12:3-6) as he does it.

records.source: וַיְהִ֧י דְבַר־יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י בַּבֹּ֥קֶר לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me in the morning, saying:
pieces: In the morning the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.8: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me in the morning, saying:

R.8: The next morning {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הֲלֹ֨א אָמְר֥וּ אֵלֶ֛יךָ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑רִי מָ֖ה אַתָּ֥ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: Son of man, [have] not said to you [the] house of Israel, the house of rebellion, What [are] you doing?
pieces: Son of man, has not the house of Israel, that rebellious house, asked you, "What are you doing?"

L.9: Son of man, has not the house of Israel, the house of rebellion, said to you, "What [are] you doing?"

R.9: Son of man, the people of Israel, who refuse to obey, have asked you, "What are you doing?"

decisions.choice: "What are you doing?": the question the sign was meant to provoke
decisions.reason: The people have watched and asked, as the sign intended (compare 24:19). The answer follows.

records.source: אֱמֹ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֑ה הַנָּשִׂ֞יא הַמַּשָּׂ֤א הַזֶּה֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔םוְכָל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֥מָּה בְתוֹכָֽם׃
records.gloss: Say to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: The prince, the oracle this, in Jerusalem, and all [the] house of Israel who [are] in its midst.
pieces: Say to them: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: This oracle is about the prince in Jerusalem and the whole house of Israel living there.

L.10: Say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: The prince [is] this oracle in Jerusalem, and all the house of Israel who [are] in its midst.

R.10: Tell them that this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: This message is about the ruler in Jerusalem and all the people of Israel who live there.

decisions.choice: the prince is this oracle: a play on "oracle" and "burden"
alternatives: this burden is the prince, the load Ezekiel carried
decisions.reason: The word for "oracle" also means "burden", something lifted and carried; both come from the verb "to lift". The words "the prince" and "the oracle" sound alike. The bundle Ezekiel lifted onto his shoulder (12:6-7) stands for the prince, who will lift his own load and go out (12:12). The plain sense is that the oracle concerns him; the pun makes him the burden itself.

decisions.choice: the prince in Jerusalem: King Zedekiah
decisions.reason: The ruler in Jerusalem at this time was Zedekiah, made king by Nebuchadnezzar in 597 BC (2 Kings 24:17). Ezekiel calls him "prince", not "king", perhaps because the exiled Jehoiachin was still counted as king (1:2; 17:12-13). The verses that follow describe Zedekiah's flight and capture.

decisions.choice: prince (L, B), ruler (R); oracle (L, B), message (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these words in the prophets and in Ezekiel. Literal keeps the bare Hebrew phrase; Balanced and Readable give its plain sense (m1).

records.source: אֱמֹ֖ר אֲנִ֣י מֽוֹפֶתְכֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֗יתִי כֵּ֚ן יֵעָשֶׂ֣ה לָהֶ֔ם בַּגּוֹלָ֥ה בַשְּׁבִ֖י יֵלֵֽכוּ׃
records.gloss: Say, I [am] your sign; as I have done, so it will be done to them; into exile, into captivity they will go.
pieces: Say: I am a sign for you. As I have done, so it will be done to them. They will go into exile, into captivity.

L.11: Say, I [am] your sign; as I have done, so it will be done to them; into exile, into captivity they will go.

R.11: Tell them: I am a sign for you. What I have done will happen to them. They will be taken away as captives into exile.

decisions.choice: I am your sign: Ezekiel himself is the message
decisions.reason: Ezekiel speaks in his own name here. What he has acted out shows what will be done to the people of Jerusalem.

records.source: וְהַנָּשִׂ֨יא אֲשֶׁר־בְּתוֹכָ֜ם אֶל־כָּתֵ֤ף יִשָּׂא֙ בָּעֲלָטָ֣ה וְיֵצֵ֔א בַּקִּ֥יר יַחְתְּר֖וּ לְה֣וֹצִיא ב֑וֹ פָּנָ֣יו יְכַסֶּ֔ה יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹא־יִרְאֶ֥ה לַעַ֛יִןה֖וּא אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And the prince who [is] in their midst on [the] shoulder will lift in the darkness and go out; through the wall they will dig to bring out through it; his face he will cover, so that not he will see with [the] eye the land.
pieces: The prince among them will lift his bundle onto his shoulder in the dark and go out. They will dig through the wall to get him out through it. He will cover his face so that he cannot see the land with his eyes.

L.12: And the prince who [is] among them will lift [his load] onto [his] shoulder in the dark and go out; through the wall they will dig to bring [him] out by it; he will cover his face, so that he may not see the land with [his] eye.

R.12: The ruler of the people will put his bundle on his shoulder and leave in the dark. A hole will be dug through the wall to get him out. He will cover his face so that he cannot see the land.

decisions.choice: the prince will go out in the dark through the wall: Zedekiah's flight from Jerusalem
decisions.reason: When the Babylonians broke into Jerusalem in 586 BC, Zedekiah and his soldiers fled by night through a gate between the two walls, toward the Jordan valley (2 Kings 25:4; Jeremiah 39:4; 52:7).

decisions.choice: so that he may not see the land: covering his face, and the blindness to come
decisions.reason: The clause may give the purpose of covering his face, or say that he will not see the land again. Either way it prepares for 12:13: he will be taken to Babylon and will not see it.

decisions.choice: A hole will be dug
decisions.reason: Readable avoids an unexplained "they".

records.source: וּפָרַשְׂתִּ֤י אֶת־רִשְׁתִּי֙ עָלָ֔יו וְנִתְפַּ֖שׂ בִּמְצֽוּדָתִ֑י וְהֵבֵאתִ֨י אֹת֤וֹ בָבֶ֨לָה֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וְאוֹתָ֥הּ לֹֽא־יִרְאֶ֖ה וְשָׁ֥ם יָמֽוּת׃
records.gloss: And I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare; and I will bring him to Babylon, [the] land of [the] Chaldeans; but it he will not see, and there he will die.
pieces: I will spread {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net over him, and he will be trapped in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} snare. I will take him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, but he will not see it, and he will die there.

L.13: And I will spread {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net over him, and he will be seized in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} snare; and I will bring him to Babylon, land of the Chaldeans; but it he will not see, and there he will die.

R.13: But I will throw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} net over him and catch him in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} trap. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Babylonians. But he will not see it, and he will die there.

decisions.choice: he will not see Babylon, and there he will die: Zedekiah was blinded before he was taken there
decisions.reason: Zedekiah was captured near Jericho and brought to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah, where his sons were killed in front of him and his eyes were put out. He was then taken to Babylon in chains and died there (2 Kings 25:5-7; Jeremiah 52:8-11).

decisions.choice: my net, my snare: the LORD himself captures the king
decisions.reason: The Babylonians caught Zedekiah, but the LORD calls the net his own, as in 17:20. The king's capture is the LORD's doing.

decisions.choice: the land of the Babylonians
decisions.reason: Readable says "Babylonians" for the Chaldeans, as the settled wording does.

records.source: וְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר סְבִיבֹתָ֥יו עֶזְר֛וֹ וְכָל־אֲגַפָּ֖יו אֱזָרֶ֣ה לְכָל־ר֑וּחַ וְחֶ֖רֶב אָרִ֥יק אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And all who [are] around him, his helpers and all his troops, I will scatter to every wind, and [the] sword I will unsheathe after them.
pieces: All those around him, his helpers and all his troops, I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw the sword to pursue them.

L.14: And all who [are] around him, his helpers and all his troops, I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw out the sword after them.

R.14: I will scatter in every direction all the people around him, his helpers and his soldiers. I will chase them with a sword.

decisions.choice: scatter to every wind and draw the sword after them: the words of 5:2, 12
decisions.reason: The same picture is used in 5:2 and 5:12. When Zedekiah was caught, his army scattered and left him (2 Kings 25:5).

decisions.choice: his troops: his bands of soldiers
decisions.reason: The word is used only by Ezekiel (17:21; 38:6, 9, 22; 39:4), always of an army's companies.

records.source: וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה בַּהֲפִיצִ֤י אוֹתָם֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם וְזֵרִיתִ֥י אוֹתָ֖ם בָּאֲרָצֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And they will know that I [am] Yahweh, when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them among the lands.
pieces: Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I scatter them among the nations and spread them across the lands.

L.15: And they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I scatter them among the nations and disperse them in the lands.

R.15: Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I scatter them among the nations and spread them through other lands.

decisions.choice: they will know that I am the LORD (see 6:7)
decisions.reason: See 6:7. Here it is the scattered people of Jerusalem who will know.

records.source: וְהוֹתַרְתִּ֤י מֵהֶם֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י מִסְפָּ֔ר מֵחֶ֖רֶב מֵרָעָ֣ב וּמִדָּ֑בֶר לְמַ֨עַן יְסַפְּר֜וּ אֶת־כָּל־תּוֹעֲבֽוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם בַּגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣אוּ שָׁ֔ם וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: But I will leave of them men few in number from [the] sword, from famine and from pestilence, so that they may recount all their abominations among the nations where they go; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: But I will spare a few of them from the sword, famine and plague, so that among the nations where they go they may tell about all their detestable practices. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.16: But I will leave a few {{gender:people|men}} of them from the sword, from famine and from pestilence, so that they may recount all their abominations among the nations where they go; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.16: But I will let a few of them live through the war, famine and disease. Then they can tell the nations where they go about all the disgusting things they did. And they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a few survivors as witnesses: their own account shows why the judgment came
decisions.reason: The few who survive will tell the nations what they did, so that the nations see that the LORD's judgment was just. The same thought returns in 14:22-23.

decisions.choice: "they will know": the survivors, or the nations who hear them
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. It may be the survivors themselves or the nations who hear their story; the verse allows both.

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence (L); sword, famine and plague (B); war, famine and disease (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this list, from the Jeremiah table.

decisions.choice: a few {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for "men" here means people; the survivors are not only men. Balanced and Readable say "a few of them", which needs no setting.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.17: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

records.heading: Bread eaten with trembling

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם לַחְמְךָ֖ בְּרַ֣עַשׁ תֹּאכֵ֑ל וּמֵימֶ֕יךָ בְּרָגְזָ֥ה וּבִדְאָגָ֖ה תִּשְׁתֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: Son of man, your bread with quaking you shall eat, and your water with trembling and with anxiety you shall drink.
pieces: Son of man, eat your food trembling, and drink your water shaking with anxiety.

L.18: Son of man, your bread you shall eat with quaking, and your water you shall drink with trembling and with anxiety.

R.18: Son of man, shake as you eat your food. Tremble with worry as you drink your water.

decisions.choice: eat with quaking, drink with trembling: a second sign, like the rationed food of 4:9-17
decisions.reason: Ezekiel is to eat and drink like a person in fear, acting out how the people of Jerusalem will live during the siege (12:19; 4:16-17).

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֶל־עַ֣ם הָאָ֡רֶץ כֹּֽה־אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה לְיוֹשְׁבֵ֤י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ אֶל־אַדְמַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַחְמָם֙ בִּדְאָגָ֣ה יֹאכֵ֔לוּ וּמֵֽימֵיהֶ֖ם בְּשִׁמָּמ֣וֹן יִשְׁתּ֑וּ לְמַ֜עַן תֵּשַׁ֤ם אַרְצָהּ֙ מִמְּלֹאָ֔הּ מֵחֲמַ֖ס כָּֽל־הַיֹּשְׁבִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And say to [the] people of the land, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh concerning [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem on [the] soil of Israel: Their bread with anxiety they will eat, and their water with horror they will drink, so that its land may be desolate of its fullness, because of [the] violence of all those living in it.
pieces: Say to the people of the land: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this about those who live in Jerusalem, in the land of Israel: They will eat their food with anxiety and drink their water in horror, for their land will be stripped of all it holds because of the violence of everyone who lives there.

L.19: And say to the people of the land, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem on the soil of Israel: Their bread they will eat with anxiety, and their water they will drink with horror, so that its land may be stripped of its fullness because of the violence of all who live in it.

R.19: Say to the people of the land: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says about the people living in Jerusalem, in the land of Israel: They will be worried as they eat their food, and terrified as they drink their water. Their land will be stripped bare because of all the violence of the people who live there.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: here, the people Ezekiel speaks to
alternatives: the landowners of Judah, as the phrase often means
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the phrase can mean the landowning citizens of Judah (2 Kings 11:14; 23:30). Here Ezekiel is told to speak to "the people of the land" about those in Jerusalem, so it probably means the people in general, the exiles around him.

decisions.choice: so that its land may be stripped of its fullness: the result of the siege, and its cause
decisions.reason: The clause gives the outcome: the land will be emptied of all it contains. "Because of the violence" gives the reason (compare 7:23; 8:17; 9:9).

decisions.choice: the soil of Israel: Ezekiel's phrase for the land (see 11:17)

records.source: וְהֶעָרִ֤ים הַנּֽוֹשָׁבוֹת֙ תֶּחֱרַ֔בְנָה וְהָאָ֖רֶץ שְׁמָמָ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֑ה וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And the cities the inhabited will be laid waste, and the land a desolation will be; and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: The cities where people live will be laid waste, and the land will become a desolation. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.20: And the inhabited cities will be laid waste, and the land will be a desolation; and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.20: The towns where people now live will be destroyed, and the land will be empty and ruined. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD (see 6:7)
decisions.reason: See 6:7.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

L.21: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

records.heading: Every vision will come true

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם מָֽה־הַמָּשָׁ֤ל הַזֶּה֙ לָכֶ֔ם עַל־אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר יַֽאַרְכוּ֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וְאָבַ֖ד כָּל־חָזֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Son of man, what [is] this proverb [that] you [have] about [the] soil of Israel, saying, Are prolonged the days, and perishes every vision?
pieces: Son of man, what is this proverb you have about the land of Israel: "The days go on and on, and every vision comes to nothing"?

L.22: Son of man, what [is] this proverb that you have about the soil of Israel, saying, "The days are drawn out, and every vision perishes"?

R.22: Son of man, why do the people of Israel keep repeating this saying about their land: "Time goes by, and none of the visions ever come true"?

decisions.choice: a proverb: a saying repeated by the people, here mocking prophecy
decisions.reason: The word can mean a proverb, a byword or a parable. This one says that because the prophets' warnings have not come true yet, they never will. A second saying follows in 12:27, and 2 Peter 3:4 answers a similar taunt.

decisions.choice: about the soil of Israel: the saying is current in the land, or concerns it
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "about" or "in". The saying belongs to the people of the land, whether in Jerusalem or among the exiles.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel keep repeating
decisions.reason: The "you" is plural, meaning the people. Readable names them.

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִשְׁבַּ֨תִּי֙ אֶת־הַמָּשָׁ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה וְלֹֽא־יִמְשְׁל֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ ע֖וֹד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֚י אִם־דַּבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם קָֽרְבוּ֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וּדְבַ֖ר כָּל־חָזֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Therefore say to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: I will make cease this proverb, and not they will use it as a proverb again in Israel. But speak to them, Are near the days and [the] word of every vision.
pieces: Therefore say to them: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I will put an end to this proverb, and they will not quote it in Israel anymore. Tell them instead: The days are near when every vision will be fulfilled.

L.23: Therefore say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: I will put an end to this proverb, and they will no longer use it as a proverb in Israel. But speak to them: The days are near, and the word of every vision.

R.23: So tell them that this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to put a stop to this saying. People in Israel will not repeat it anymore. Instead, tell them: The time is near when every vision will come true.

decisions.choice: the days are near, and the word of every vision: the fulfillment of every vision
decisions.reason: "Word" here means the thing spoken of, the event itself. The answer turns the proverb around: not "the days are drawn out" but "the days are near"; not "every vision perishes" but "every vision's word" is at hand.

decisions.choice: when every vision will be fulfilled (B); when every vision will come true (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the word of every vision" means (m1).

records.source: כִּ֠י לֹ֣א יִֽהְיֶ֥ה ע֛וֹד כָּל־חֲז֥וֹן שָׁ֖וְא וּמִקְסַ֣ם חָלָ֑ק בְּת֖וֹךְ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: For there will not be again any vision of falsehood or divination smooth in [the] midst of [the] house of Israel.
pieces: For there will be no more false visions or flattering divination among the house of Israel.

L.24: For there will no longer be any empty vision or flattering divination in the midst of the house of Israel.

R.24: Prophets in Israel will no longer have false visions or tell people only what they want to hear.

decisions.choice: empty vision and flattering divination: false prophecy that tells people what they want to hear
decisions.reason: "Empty" means worthless or false. Divination, seeking hidden knowledge by signs and omens, was forbidden in Israel (Deuteronomy 18:10-14); here the word brands the false prophets' messages, which Ezekiel attacks in chapter 13 (13:6-7, 23). "Flattering" is literally "smooth" (compare Isaiah 30:10).

decisions.choice: tell people only what they want to hear
decisions.reason: Readable says what this kind of divination did, without the technical word (m1).

records.source: כִּ֣י׀אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֲדַבֵּר֙ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲדַבֵּ֤ר דָּבָר֙ וְיֵ֣עָשֶׂ֔ה לֹ֥א תִמָּשֵׁ֖ךְ ע֑וֹד כִּ֣י בִֽימֵיכֶ֞ם בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֗רִי אֲדַבֵּ֤ר דָּבָר֙ וַעֲשִׂיתִ֔יו נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: For I [am] Yahweh: I will speak what I will speak, [the] word, and it will be done; not it will be delayed again. For in your days, house of rebellion, I will speak a word and do it, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: For I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will speak whatever word I speak, and it will be done without further delay. In your own days, you rebellious house, I will speak the word and carry it out, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.25: For I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: I will speak whatever word I speak, and it will be done; it will not be delayed any longer. For in your days, house of rebellion, I will speak a word and do it, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.25: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. When I speak, what I say will happen. It will not be put off any longer. You people who refuse to obey, while you are still alive I will say what will happen, and I will make it happen, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: for I am the LORD: I will speak
alternatives: for I, the LORD, will speak
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a statement ("I am the LORD") followed by what he will do, or as "I, the LORD, will speak". The sense is the same: the LORD's word is not like the empty visions of 12:24.

decisions.choice: in your days: within your own lifetime
decisions.reason: The fulfillment is not for distant generations (as 12:27 claims) but for those now living.

decisions.choice: house of rebellion (L); you rebellious house (B); You people who refuse to obey (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this phrase (see 2:5), here as a form of address.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.26: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם הִנֵּ֤ה בֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֹֽמְרִ֔ים הֶחָז֛וֹן אֲשֶׁר־ה֥וּא חֹזֶ֖ה לְיָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וּלְעִתִּ֥ים רְחוֹק֖וֹת ה֥וּא נִבָּֽא׃
records.gloss: Son of man, behold, [the] house of Israel [are] saying, The vision that he sees [is] for days many, and for times far off he prophesies.
pieces: Son of man, the house of Israel is saying, "The vision he sees is for many days to come; he prophesies about times far away."

L.27: Son of man, look, the house of Israel are saying, "The vision that he is seeing [is] for many days [from now], and of times far off he prophesies."

R.27: Son of man, the people of Israel are saying, "The visions he sees will not come true for a long time. He is talking about things that will happen far in the future."

decisions.choice: "for many days, for times far off": a second saying, which puts the prophecy off rather than denying it
decisions.reason: The first saying (12:22) claimed that visions come to nothing. This one grants that Ezekiel's visions may come true, but not in their time, so they need not change. The LORD's answer is the same (12:28).

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה לֹא־תִמָּשֵׁ֥ךְ ע֖וֹד כָּל־דְּבָרָ֑י אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲדַבֵּ֤ר דָּבָר֙ וְיֵ֣עָשֶׂ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Therefore say to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Not it will be delayed again, any of my words; [the] word that I speak, and it will be done, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: Therefore say to them: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: None of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words will be put off any longer. Whatever I say will be done, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.28: Therefore say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: None of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words will be delayed any longer; the word that I speak will be done, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.28: So tell them that this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Nothing I have said will be put off any longer. What I say will happen, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: none of my words will be delayed: the promise of 12:25 repeated
decisions.reason: The answer to both sayings is the same: what the LORD has said will happen, and soon.
